items.title: Rick Montalbano interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 12, 2011
items.q: You can stretch out behind them. Sal, once he started playing he didn’t need anything.

ctx.x: I know you’ve mentioned one thing that I think you very much like is when a horn player or a singer has their own sense of time. You used to tell me to listen to Dolores [Mancuso] how she, and Sal Amico too.

Right. Yes. Yeah. Those are people, you don’t have to make the box for. They’re in the box by themselves. We are all sharing the same concept. So you can do what you have to. You don’t have to feel obligated to square everything off and set a foundation for them. So it makes it more interesting and more fun to play that way. You can stretch out behind them. Sal, once he started playing he didn’t need anything.
Once he started playing. I remember I used to watch him and he’d just be going [soft scatting], and then all of a sudden like, oh, when did the song start?
